issues.legal_issue: A higher court should not ordinarily interfere at an interlocutory stage to quash pending criminal proceedings when deciding the disputed issue requires evidence.
material_facts: The accused were being prosecuted for allegedly failing to employ a qualified geologist or mining engineer in connection with mineral extraction.
They sought to quash the prosecution on the ground that the extracted stone was a minor mineral excluded from the relevant rules.
The trial court rejected their preliminary objection, and the High Court declined to quash the proceedings.
The case was at its threshold, and evidence had not yet been adduced on whether the extracted mineral could be used as a major mineral for certain purposes.
issues.conclusion: The Court dismissed the appeal, declined to interfere with the refusal to quash the proceedings, and left the accused free to raise any available defence before the trial court.
issues.legal_principle: A High Court does not ordinarily interfere under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, with criminal proceedings pending in a subordinate court at an interlocutory stage. The Supreme Court likewise will not ordinarily exercise its extraordinary jurisdiction under Article 136 to intervene when the case is at its threshold and the disputed question cannot properly be determined in the abstract without relevant evidence. No earlier cases were relied on.

predicates.appeal_challenges_refusal_of_early_quash: The accused appealed after a court refused to terminate pending criminal proceedings at an early stage.
predicates.criminal_proceedings_pending_in_lower_co: The criminal proceedings remained pending before a lower court when the challenged decision was made.
predicates.disputed_classification_requires_evidenc: The disputed classification of the material depended on evidence that had not yet been adduced.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges an early refusal to terminate pending criminal proceedings and the disputed classification requires evidence, the appeal is dismissed while the accused remain free to raise their defences in the lower court.
